label: What the quick start does
content: The Busymate AI quick start lets a visitor type ANY website address into busymate.ai and see, in one click, what their mate would look like on that exact site. It fetches the public pages of the given host, builds a grounded assistant preview from that content, and opens it at busymate.ai/try/<host>. No account, no sign-up form, and no credit card at any point in the flow.

label: No sign-up, one click
content: The quick start never asks for an email, a password, or payment details before showing a result. It is exactly one click: paste the URL, press the button, and the preview assistant plus the scorecard load in the same page. A visitor can try as many sites as they want, with no rate limit that requires an account, and can leave at any time with nothing saved server-side unless they choose to continue.

label: The AI-readiness scorecard
content: Alongside the assistant preview, the quick start runs an AI-readiness scorecard against the scanned site: whether it publishes an llms.txt file, an agents.json manifest, exposes an MCP server for structured data, offers WebMCP page tools a browser agent can call, and whether its pages carry clean structured data (JSON-LD), a robots.txt that allows AI crawlers by name, and a sitemap.xml. Each check on the scorecard links to the specific guide that explains how to add it, at busymate.ai/docs/guides. The same scorecard that runs on a prospect's site also runs on this demo page itself, at busymate.ai/try/scan.demo.busymate.ai.

label: What it costs
content: Running the quick start and viewing the scorecard is completely free and does not require a plan. If a visitor wants to keep the assistant live on their own site with their own knowledge, channels, and usage limits, plans and pricing are published at busymate.ai/pricing — the quick start itself never charges anything and never requires a card to try.

label: Human hand-off
content: Every Busymate AI assistant, including Beacon, can hand a conversation off to a real person when it cannot help. In the chat widget on this demo page, type "talk to a human" or "I need a person" and the assistant will offer to connect the conversation to the support team instead of guessing at an answer.
